angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 322,805 km at 42.48 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 23.5387 +/- 0.0151 mas (same row, RUWE 1.27): 42.48 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.464 +/- 0.013 solar radii from Fukui et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2285 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022PASJ...74L...1F/abstract): 322,805 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.454 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Fukui et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2285 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022PASJ...74L...1F/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3491 +/- 58 K from Fukui et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2285 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022PASJ...74L...1F/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Fukui et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2285 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022PASJ...74L...1F/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2285.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.762, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
